title: Adaptive lane throttling and staged degradation profiles for multi-region failover
creator: Maya Rivera
description: Problem: During cross-region incidents we observe cascading latency and errors as transiently overloaded regions begin forwarding traffic. Existing shedding strategies are static (per-tenant token buckets or single priority lanes) and lead to either unnecessary failed requests or long tail latency for high-priority tenants. This ticket proposes an adaptive lane throttling system that combines dynamic admission control with staged degradation profiles to preserve SLOs and maintain graceful behavior across multi-region failovers.
rationale: We need a mechanism that: 1) keeps critical tenants within their SLO during spikes and failovers, 2) prevents cascading overload when a region forwards traffic, and 3) allows controlled fidelity reductions (e.g., token/response slimming, model variant fallback) as a safe degradation path. Adaptive lanes let us reassign request classes based on live signals (latency percentiles, queue sizes, KV cache hit rates) and apply pre-configured degradation profiles per lane.
design_decisions:
- Use three lane classes: express (latency-sensitive), standard (default), and soft (best-effort).
- Admission control uses per-lane leaky buckets with dynamic capacity derived from short-window P99 latency and CPU/GPU scheduling headroom.
- Implement staged degradation profiles as ordered actions: 1) request thinning (probabilistic rejection), 2) response slimming (truncate tokens/disable sampling-heavy features), 3) model variant fallback (quantized/smaller model), 4) queued retry/backoff.
- Placement: control-plane policy computed in region leader, applied locally to per-node admission controllers.
- Safety: global circuit breaker monitors cross-region error rates and flips conservative policy (higher rejection thresholds) when forwarding volume > 20% baseline.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: preserves P99 for express lane, predictable SLO behavior, finer control over user experience.
- Cons: added complexity to control plane, potential for noisy policy oscillation if signals are too reactive, risk of customer confusion if fidelity reductions are not surfaced.
- Mitigations: smoothing windows, minimum hold times for policy changes, explicit telemetry labels to attribute degradation to system actions.
implementation_plan:
1) Instrument signals: queue depths, P50/P95/P99 per lane, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate (2 days).
2) Build per-node admission-controller shim supporting leaky bucket + probabilistic thinning and a policy API (2 sprints).
3) Implement staged degradation handlers in serving runtime (slimming, variant switch) and expose flags for A/B (3 sprints).
4) Control-plane policy service: lane capacity calculator and region leader arbitration (2 sprints).
5) E2E tests + chaos scenarios (multi-region failover replay) and gradual rollout (canary -> 20% -> global) (2 sprints).
rollout_plan:
- Canary in single non-critical region with synthetic load and a small set of internal tenants.
- Expand to additional regions with progressive percentage ramp and rollback triggers based on P99 and error-budget burn.
- Release notes and deprecation guidance for customers that rely on strict per-tenant throughput.
- Enable by default with opt-out via tenant-level flags for first month of rollout.
monitoring_and_slos:
- New metrics: lane_capacity_utilization, lane_rejections_total, staged_degradation_actions_total{action=slim|fallback|thin}, policy_changes/sec, cross_region_forward_rate.
- Dashboards: per-region lane heatmap and SLO burn rate with alerting on minute-scale P99 > target or staged_degradation_actions_total surge.
- SLO impact: design target is to keep express lane P99 within current SLO during 95% of simulated failovers; degradation should first affect soft lane availability.
- Alerts: automated rollback if error budget consumption > 2x baseline for 10m or if customer-facing error rate increases > 0.5% absolute.

acceptance_criteria: Per-node admission controller that supports leaky buckets and probabilistic thinning is merged and deployed to canary cluster.
Staged degradation handlers (slim, variant-fallback) are implemented with feature flags and unit tests.
Control-plane policy calculator is capable of computing per-lane capacity and enforces minimum hold times and hysteresis.
End-to-end chaos run simulating region failure shows express lane P99 within SLO for 95% of runs and soft lane bears >70% of rejections.
Runbook and dashboards published with alert thresholds and rollback procedures.
